More modern use is in an orchestra or another ensemble, where all the strings play a single melodic line. It sounds as a chordophone and is played with a pick, like the mandolin and the baglama; it is also connected with the line-up of the tamburica orchestra.

Its range is usually the middle and lower register, with a deep and lasting resonance. The vibrating strings give rich overtones, so the sound is clearly layered, and the overall timbre has a still, far-reaching quality.

The body is mostly wooden: the Bulgarian body is often carved from a single piece of wood, while the Macedonian is more often built up from staves, like a lute. Both have a floating bridge and a metal tailpiece, and a long slim neck with frets set for the Western twelve-note scale. The source does not state the materials of the other parts.

Its earliest forms can be traced to Persia and the Arab lands, and it later reached India, where it became an important accompanying instrument in Indian classical music.

The player uses particular plucking patterns to produce a continuous harmony that gives the leading instrument a musical background to stand on. In Indian traditional music the tambura is used mainly to hold the pitch and the beat, and it is an indispensable accompanying instrument in the Hindu classical music system.

The tambura is a chordophone of the Balkans, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322. As a folk instrument it is common in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia (especially Vojvodina) and Slovenia. It has a long, narrow neck, usually with eighteen to twenty-four frets, and steel strings in pairs; it is played with a pick, in the same way as the mandolin and the baglama.
相較於古典吉他的清晰透亮，坦布拉琴音色更顯厚實溫暖；相比琵琶的剛烈有力，其音質則: Beside the clear, bright classical guitar the tambura sounds fuller and warmer; beside the fierce power of the pipa its tone is soft and held in. The resonator naturally lengthens the decay of each note, so the sound keeps on pulsing. That makes it an ideal accompanying instrument, giving a steady musical foundation and atmosphere in the South Asian classical tradition.
隨著全球化發展，坦布拉琴的影響力逐漸擴展至西方音樂圈。許多世界音樂愛好者和音樂學: As globalisation went on, the tambura's influence gradually spread into Western music circles. Many world-music enthusiasts and musicologists began to study and play the instrument, so that it became a bridge between cultures and holds an important place in contemporary world music.
